items.title: Actual generic regularity for distinct-end strips with fixed endpoint collars
items.scope_note: All actual distinct-end strips simultaneously, and all actual real-Fredholm-index1 strips between oriented product tori. Actualoperator index not yet identified with unproveddomainMaslovformula. Genuine commonendpointcollars/protectedvalues retained.
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the actual smooth Hilbert family of almost complex paths with fixed endpoint collars, fixed totally real boundary structures, exact product generator charts, and compact transverse boundary submanifolds. Write $\mathcal K=L_0\cap L_1$, a finite set. Make the following separated choice of its spatial protected set: for every $x\in\mathcal K$ choose a compact neighborhood $A_x$ of $x$ inside its product generator chart, with the $A_x$ pairwise disjoint, and choose a compact protected set $D$ disjoint from their union. Set
$$P=\bigl(([0,\eta]\cup[1-\eta,1])\times X\bigr)\ \cup\ \bigl([0,1]\times(D\cup\bigcup_{x\in\mathcal K}A_x)\bigr).$$
Here the background path is constant on the stated endpoint collars, exact product-integrable near each $A_x$, and has any required protected diagonal and divisor values on $D$. Use the constructed Hilbert family with this $P$ and any tameness conditions in that construction.

A dense residual subset of its parameter ball consists of parameters $a$ for which the actual geometric $H^1\to L^2$ linearization is surjective at every smooth finite-energy $J_t(a)$ strip whose end generators are distinct. The same operator is surjective in every integer higher Hilbert Sobolev realization. The universal derivative is onto at every such actual strip, and the actual universal solution space and Fredholm parameter projection are thereby supplied.

For oriented product tori, this same residual set gives surjectivity at every actual strip of real Fredholm index one, including all choices of end generators: a same-generator strip has even real index. This assertion concerns the actual operator index and does not supply its identification with a separate domain or relative grading formula.

Every path in this conclusion is constant on the same actual endpoint collars and retains all specified protected values. The theorem covers all actual distinct-end strips simultaneously, without a hypothesis that their homotopy classes have already been enumerated. It does not cover nonconstant strips with the same end generator, does not assert compactness of any fixed-index moduli space, and does not exclude sphere or boundary-degeneration strata. Those remain separate obligations for the full pointed Floer analytic result.

items.title: The real-boundary strip operator with free end constants and its exact matching condition
items.scope_note: Same-generator index2 genericity/supportavailability, full domainMaslov/Euler identification, multipointed lowindexsphere/boundarydegeneration classification and actual count/gluing/cancellation, polygons/continuation remain. Frozenfirst38 independentcycle1 no confirmeddefect; source39and40 remain outside that review.
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $S=\mathbb R_s\times[0,1]_t$ and $m\ge1$. Let $\mathcal X_{\mathbb R}^1$ be the real $H^1$ completion of smooth maps compactly supported in $s$ with values in $\mathbb R^m$ on both horizontal edges. Choose a smooth $\rho\ge0$ equal to $|s|$ for $|s|\ge1$, with $|\rho'|\le1$ and bounded derivatives of every positive order, and let $w=e^{\delta\rho}$ for $0<\delta<\pi$. Put $H^q_\delta=w^{-1}H^q$ and $\mathcal X^1_{\mathbb R,\delta}=w^{-1}\mathcal X^1_{\mathbb R}$. Fix a smooth real cutoff $\chi_+$ equal to zero for $s\le-1$ and one for $s\ge1$, and put $\chi_-=1-\chi_+$.

For every integer $q\ge0$ define the real Hilbert domain of maps with free real end constants by
$$\mathcal E_q=\{u=r+\chi_-c_-+\chi_+c_+:\ r\in H^{q+1}_\delta\cap\mathcal X^1_{\mathbb R,\delta},\ c_-,c_+\in\mathbb R^m\},$$
with norm $\|wr\|_{H^{q+1}}+|c_-|+|c_+|$ or its equivalent squared-sum Hilbert norm. This representation is unique. The actual operator
$$D_0=\partial_s+i\partial_t:\mathcal E_q\longrightarrow H^q_\delta$$
is bounded and onto, has kernel exactly the global real constant maps, and has real Fredholm index $m$. It has a specified bounded right inverse $Q_q$ whose solutions have $c_-=0$; these right inverses agree on their common domains. For $u\in\mathcal E_0$ and $f=D_0u$, the exact matching identity is
$$c_+-c_-=\int_{\mathbb R}f_0(s)\,ds,\qquad f_0(s)=\operatorname{Re}\int_0^1 f(s,t)\,dt.$$
In particular a solution with both end constants zero exists exactly when this real integral is zero, and is then unique. At higher orders only the zeroth real boundary trace is imposed; no normal-derivative or forcing trace is added. This is the actual linear same-boundary neck model. It asserts no geometric boundary-degeneration classification or nonlinear gluing theorem.

items.title: A generator-attached boundary disk has an actual exponential end and two affine kernel directions
items.scope_note: Actual supplied nonconstant finiteenergy autonomousJdisk attached atgenerator with exactintegrable/realchart. No curveddisk regularity, Fredholmindex formula, classification, counts, or nonlinear gluing inferred.
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,J)$ be compact with smooth almost complex structure, $L\subset X$ compact and totally real, and let $u:\overline{\mathbb H}\to X$ be a smooth nonconstant $J$-holomorphic map of finite Dirichlet energy with $u(\mathbb R)\subset L$. At the source boundary puncture $\infty$, let its removable value be $x\in L$. Suppose a fixed complex-coordinate neighborhood $q$ about $x$ identifies $J$ exactly with $i$ and $L$ exactly with $\mathbb R^m$, with $q(x)=0$. This is the local situation for a disk attached at a generator with a fixed product-integrable generator chart.

In the compactifying coordinate $w=-1/z$ there is a convergent holomorphic expansion
$$q(u(-1/w))=\sum_{n\ge k}a_nw^n,\qquad a_n\in\mathbb R^m,\qquad a_k\ne0,\qquad k\ge1.$$
Thus in the positive cylindrical end coordinate $z=e^{\pi(s+it)}$, $t\in[0,1]$, the actual map has, for every derivative order $j$, a bound
$$|D^j q(u(e^{\pi(s+it)}))|\le C_j e^{-\pi k s}.$$
Its coordinate difference from $x$ belongs to every $H^j_\delta$ on the end for every $0<\delta<\pi k$, using any smooth weight equal to $e^{\delta s}$ there.

The actual geometric linearized equation along the disk, with boundary tangent to $L$ and section value zero at the marked boundary point $\infty$, has two linearly independent smooth solution sections
$$\xi_{\rm tr}(z)=du_z(1),\qquad \xi_{\rm dil}(z)=du_z(z).$$
They are the derivatives of the actual precompositions $u(z+b)$ and $u(e^a z)$ for real $b,a$. In the target chart at the node their expressions are $w^2v'(w)$ and $-wv'(w)$, respectively, where $v(w)=q(u(-1/w))$. Their cylindrical derivatives of every fixed order decay at rates $\pi(k+1)$ and $\pi k$, respectively. Both sections therefore lie in every smooth compact-disk Sobolev space with this zeroth boundary condition, and in the corresponding exponentially weighted cylindrical spaces below those rates. This supplies actual affine reparametrization kernel directions, not surjectivity or a count of boundary degenerations.

items.title: An actual oriented totally real disk operator is Fredholm in every integer Hilbert realization
items.scope_note: Actual smoothcomplexbundle overcompactdisk and orientedsmoothtotrealboundary. H1boundarycompletion and higherweakSobolev intersections precisely distinguished. No surjectivity, Heegaarddomainindex, puncture or gluing assertion.
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $E\to\overline{\mathbb D}$ be a smooth complex vector bundle of rank $m\ge1$, with complex multiplication $J$, and let $F\subset E|_{\partial\mathbb D}$ be a smooth oriented totally real real subbundle of rank $m$. Let $P$ be a smooth real-linear first-order operator on sections with exact Cauchy–Riemann symbol: for real smooth $h$ and smooth $\xi$,
$$P(h\xi)=hP\xi+h_x\xi+h_yJ\xi.$$
Use smooth positive definite metrics and finite smooth charts to define $H^r(E)$ by weak derivatives for integers $r\ge1$. Let $X_0$ be the $H^1$ closure of smooth sections with boundary values in $F$, and put $X_q=H^{q+1}(E)\cap X_0$, $Y_q=H^q(E)$ for integers $q\ge0$. Only the zeroth boundary condition is imposed.

There is a smooth global complex frame of $E$ and an integer $k$ in which the boundary condition is
$$F(e^{it})=e^{ikt}\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb R^{m-1}$$
and the actual operator is $\partial_x+i\partial_y+B$ with smooth real-linear zeroth-order coefficient $B$. Equivalently, before this reduction, if $C(t)$ is the complex matrix whose columns are any smooth periodic oriented real frame of $F$ in any global complex frame, then
$$k=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_0^{2\pi}\frac{(\det C)'(t)}{\det C(t)}\,dt.$$
Such frames exist, and this integer is independent of both choices.

Every actual realization $P_q:X_q\to Y_q$ is bounded Fredholm with real index $m+2k$. Its kernel is the same set as the $H^1$ kernel, its range is $Y_q\cap\operatorname{Ran}P_0$, and inclusion in $L^2$ identifies its real cokernel with that of $P_0$. For $\xi\in X_0$ and $P\xi=f\in H^q$,
$$\|\xi\|_{H^{q+1}}\le C_q(\|f\|_{H^q}+\|\xi\|_{H^1}).$$
The inverse of $P_0$ from its $H^1$ kernel complement to its closed range is bounded, and its restriction gives a bounded range inverse $H^q\cap\operatorname{Ran}P_0\to X_q$. The statement applies to an actual geometric linearization along a smooth disk with oriented totally real boundary. It does not assert its surjectivity, compute a Heegaard domain formula, or supply a puncture or gluing theorem.

items.title: A generator-punctured boundary disk has actual weighted Fredholm realizations and node evaluation
items.scope_note: Exact node Pdisk=D0/F=R, 0<delta<pi. Allintegerpuncturedweightedspaces distinguished from unweightedcompacthigherSobolev. items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the actual oriented totally real compact-disk operator $P$ of the geometric disk Fredholm theorem. Let its rank be $m$ and its boundary winding integer be $k$, so its actual compact $H^1\to L^2$ index is $m+2k$. Choose a marked boundary point $p$. Suppose a holomorphic boundary coordinate $w$ centered at $p$, and a smooth complex bundle frame near it, identify the boundary with $\mathbb R^m$ and the actual local operator with $D_0=\partial_{\operatorname{Re}w}+i\partial_{\operatorname{Im}w}$. Operator and forcing components in a changed source coordinate use the Cauchy–Riemann symbol transformation. This exact local hypothesis holds for a boundary disk attached in a fixed product-integrable generator chart.

Write $w=-e^{-\pi\zeta}$, $\zeta=s+it$, $t\in[0,1]$, for its positive cylindrical end. If $f_w$ is the local disk forcing, its cylindrical component is
$$f_{\rm cyl}(s,t)=\overline{\frac{dw}{d\zeta}}\,f_w(w).$$
Fix $0<\delta<\pi$. For an integer $q\ge0$ let $Y_{q,\delta}$ consist of forcings which are weak $H^q$ on a fixed compact source core and have $e^{\delta s}f_{\rm cyl}\in H^q$ on the end. Let $X_{q,\delta}$ consist of sections in the actual compact-disk $H^1$ boundary domain which are weak $H^{q+1}$ on that core and, on the end, have the unique form
$$\xi_{\rm cyl}=c+r,\qquad c\in\mathbb R^m,\qquad e^{\delta s}r\in H^{q+1}.$$
Use the sum-of-squares core, weighted-end and $|c|$ norms. These spaces are Hilbert; changing the fixed core cutoff gives equivalent norms. Only the original zeroth real boundary condition is imposed.

The actual weighted realization $P_{q,\delta}:X_{q,\delta}\to Y_{q,\delta}$ is Fredholm of real index $m+2k$. Its kernel equals the actual compact-disk $H^1$ kernel, its range is $Y_{q,\delta}\cap\operatorname{Ran}P_{\rm compact}$, and inclusion in compact-disk $L^2$ identifies its cokernel with the compact-disk cokernel. Its range has a specified bounded right inverse obtained by restricting the compact operator's range inverse. More precisely any compact $H^1$ solution of $P\xi=f\in Y_{q,\delta}$ lies in $X_{q,\delta}$ and satisfies
$$\|\xi\|_{X_{q,\delta}}\le C_{q,\delta}\bigl(\|f\|_{Y_{q,\delta}}+\|\xi\|_{H^1(\mathbb D)}\bigr).$$
The asymptotic constant map $\operatorname{ev}_p:\xi\mapsto c$ is bounded and onto $\mathbb R^m$. On its kernel the weighted operator is Fredholm of index $2k$, with a bounded right inverse on its actual range. For $q\ge1$ the constant is the actual continuous node value; on homogeneous solutions it is the smooth compact-disk value for every $q$. At level $q=0$, its definition is the weighted asymptotic decomposition and does not assume that an arbitrary $H^1$ section is pointwise continuous. These punctured higher spaces are not being identified with higher unweighted compact-disk Sobolev spaces. The theorem supplies neither surjectivity of the node-fixed operator nor nonlinear boundary-bubble gluing.

items.title: A holomorphic symmetric-product curve has a finite branched ordered lift even inside the diagonal
items.scope_note: Actual globallyJ0-holomorphicmap fromclosedRiemannsurface intoSymm, includingwhollydiagonal/repeatedfixedcoordinates. Not claiming arbitrarynearlysymmetriccompactbubble energy/positivity yet; those followonlyafterseparatecompactmap/divisor proof.
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $C$ be a connected closed Riemann surface, $\Sigma$ a closed Riemann surface, and $u:C\to\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$ holomorphic for the standard complex symmetric-product structure, $m\ge1$. Let $q:\Sigma^m\to\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$ be the quotient. No assumption that the image avoids or is not contained in the repeated-point locus is made.

There are a finite set $B\subset C$, a positive integer $d\le m!$, a compact possibly disconnected Riemann surface $F$, a degree-$d$ holomorphic branched covering $p:F\to C$, and a holomorphic map $\widetilde u:F\to\Sigma^m$ with
$$q\circ\widetilde u=u\circ p.$$
Over $C\setminus B$ the covering is unbranched and its fiber is exactly the finite set of distinct orderings of the tuple $u(z)$, including its repeated entries. Near every point above $B$, in suitable source coordinates the map $p$ is $\zeta\mapsto\zeta^r$ for an integer $r\ge1$, and all coordinate maps of $\widetilde u$ extend holomorphically through $\zeta=0$. In particular this lift exists for a curve lying wholly in the diagonal, including nonreduced tuples with a fixed repeated coordinate.

The proof also gives the following local fact. A monic polynomial with holomorphic one-variable coefficient germs admits, on a sufficiently small punctured disk, a locally holomorphic collection of distinct roots with constant multiplicities. Those roots extend holomorphically after finite monodromy power substitutions, even when the original polynomial has an identically vanishing discriminant.

items.title: Symmetric-product divisor intersections remain defined under point movement and divisor containment
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed connected Riemann surface, $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$ with its standard complex structure, and $m\ge1$. For $a\in\Sigma$ put $E_a=\{a\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}(\Sigma)$. This is a smooth complex hypersurface, including at repeated tuples. The universal incidence hypersurface $\mathcal E=\{(a,D):D\in E_a\}\subset\Sigma\times X$ carries a smooth complex divisor line bundle with its canonical section, whose zero set is $\mathcal E$ with multiplicity one.

For a smooth map $v:S\to X$, where $S$ is an oriented sphere or a closed disk, define $n_a(v)$ as the degree of the pullback point-divisor line bundle; for a disk use the canonical section to trivialize it on the boundary, and require $v(\partial S)\cap E_a=\varnothing$. The proof constructs this integer by elementary frame winding. It is defined even when a sphere lies wholly in $E_a$.

For a sphere, $n_a(v)$ is independent of $a$ on all of $\Sigma$. For a disk whose boundary tuples have all entries in a finite union of curves $\Gamma\subset\Sigma$, it is independent of $a$ on each connected component of $\Sigma\setminus\Gamma$. If $v^{-1}(E_a)$ is finite and the map is holomorphic on a neighborhood of every one of these points, then
$$n_a(v)=\sum_{z\in v^{-1}(E_a)}\operatorname{ord}_z(F_a\circ v)\ge0,$$
where $F_a$ is any local holomorphic defining function of the smooth hypersurface $E_a$. Each term is a positive integer. Thus the degree agrees with proper holomorphic intersection multiplicity, while divisor containment is handled by its degree definition and actual point movement rather than an unsupported proper-intersection assumption.

items.title: Compact nearly symmetric sphere and one-torus disk bubbles have positive domains and domain-controlled energy
items.scope_note: Individual compact bubbles with the requisite zero marked degrees are constant. No assertion that degrees of a zero-mark sequence already split over its limit; that additivity is the next separate authoring obligation.
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed connected Riemann surface with positive area form $\eta$, and let $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$, $m\ge1$, with standard complex structure $J_0$, quotient $q:\Sigma^m\to X$, and repeated-point locus $\Delta$. Off $\Delta$, the product form $\Omega=\sum_l\operatorname{pr}_l^*\eta$ descends to $\omega$. Fix a smooth target metric $g$ and finitely many attaching curves with finitely many complementary regions $R$. A product torus $L_\gamma$ uses one point on each of a labeled system of $m$ pairwise disjoint curves $\gamma_i$ among those curves. Choose a point $a_R$ in each region. Suppose a smooth path $J_t$ agrees with $J_0$ on a fixed neighborhood $V$ of $\Delta$ and on a fixed neighborhood of every $E_{a_R}=\{a_R\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}\Sigma$, and tames $\omega$ on $X\setminus V$.

Let $u$ be a smooth $J_\tau$-holomorphic map for any fixed $\tau\in[0,1]$, either from the oriented sphere, or from a compact disk with its entire boundary on $L_\gamma$. Let $n_R(u)=n_{a_R}(u)$ be the actual absolute or relative divisor degree constructed by the point-divisor intersection lemma. Then every $n_R(u)$ is a nonnegative integer, and a constant $C$ depending only on the fixed geometry and path satisfies
$$E_g(u)\le C\sum_R n_R(u)\int_R\eta.$$
This includes spheres lying entirely in $\Delta$ or in a point divisor; no off-diagonal-end hypothesis is present.

For a sphere all region coefficients equal one nonnegative integer $d_0$, and $n_a(u)=d_0$ for every $a\in\Sigma$. For a one-torus disk, let $A_i$ be the connected components of $\Sigma\setminus\bigcup_j\gamma_j$. Its coefficient function is constant on each $A_i$, say $b_i\ge0$, and its domain is $\sum_i b_i[A_i]$; in particular its boundary has only $\gamma$ curves. If one marked point $z_i$ is chosen in each $A_i$ away from all attaching curves, then $n_{z_i}(u)=b_i$.

Consequently a sphere with one zero point-divisor degree is constant. A one-torus disk with all the degrees $n_{z_i}$ zero is constant. The disk conclusion uses one marked point in each actual complement component, as provided by a complete marked cut system, and does not require any admissibility assertion about two-torus periodic domains or a Maslov-index formula. Applying them to a zero-mark degeneration still requires a proved additivity statement for the divisor degrees of its limiting components.

items.title: Divisor degrees split over actual bubble trees and zero-marked strips have no bubbles
items.scope_note: Genuine zero-marked strip bubble exclusion and unbubbled finite breaking under the actual compactness hypotheses, valid for general closed surface/marked cut systems without an S3 or torsion SpinC restriction. This does not infer non-torsion same-end index-two regularity from ordinary weak admissibility.
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Put $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m\Sigma$ for a closed connected Riemann surface, and fix finitely many product tori $L_j$ from systems of pairwise disjoint attaching curves. Let $a\in\Sigma$ lie off all these curves. The actual point-divisor bundle of $E_a=\{a\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}\Sigma$, with its canonical section on the boundary, defines integer degrees $n_a$ for disks and spheres, including contained spheres. It also defines an integer for every smooth strip between two transverse specified tori, with simultaneous product generator charts and uniform ends at their intersections: truncate and cap its ends inside sufficiently small generator charts avoiding $E_a$. The integer is independent of the sufficiently remote cuts and these local caps, and agrees with proper holomorphic intersection multiplicity whenever the latter is defined.

In the actual bounded-energy compactness conclusions of the bordered-source bubble-tree theorem, when the fixed source is a disk, or of the bubbled transverse-strip breaking theorem, these degrees satisfy, for all sufficiently large sequence indices,
$$n_a(u_n)=\sum_{\text{base or strip levels }v}n_a(v)+\sum_{\text{bubble components }w}n_a(w).$$
The hypotheses of those compactness theorems, including their common exact transverse generator charts for strips, are retained. No avoidance of $E_a$ by interior nodes or sphere bubbles is required. The formula holds simultaneously for any fixed finite set of such points.

In particular suppose the strip sequence satisfies that transverse-strip compactness theorem and the compact-bubble domain-energy lemma, with common diagonal and region-divisor neighborhoods and uniformly bounded geometric constants. Let $z_1,\ldots,z_k$ be marked points off all attaching curves, with $J_{n,t}$ and its limit equal to the standard symmetric-product structure near their divisors. Require that each connected component of the complement of each individual boundary curve system contains at least one of these marked points. If $n_{z_i}(u_n)=0$ for every $i,n$, its limit has no nonconstant sphere or disk bubbles. In fact no bubble vertices remain after discarding redundant constant vertices, and every retained strip level is nonconstant and has $n_{z_i}=0$ for every $i$. Thus that actual compactness theorem reduces to finite breaking of unbubbled zero-marked strips, with its smooth local convergence and full energy and neck-collapse conclusions. This does not assert regularity of same-generator index-two strips, a Maslov/domain-index identity, low-index stratum dimensions, or gluing.

items.title: All-strip universal regularity in an auxiliary flat-endpoint-jet family
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Fix compact transverse strip data with finite generator set $K=L_0\cap L_1$, and a smooth background path $J_t^b$ constant on endpoint collars, with fixed totally real boundary structures and exact all-$t$ charts taking the two boundaries to $\mathbb R^m,i\mathbb R^m$ and $J_t^b$ to $i$. Choose pairwise disjoint compact neighborhoods $A_x$ of the generators inside those charts and a compact set $D$ disjoint from their union. Choose smaller working generator charts with closures inside $\operatorname{Int}(A_x)$. All references to preserved exact generator charts below mean these smaller working charts; the original larger background charts remain available to analyze a strip whose entire image lies in $A_x$. Put $P_X=D\cup\bigcup_xA_x$, and require all desired spatially protected values on $P_X$. For an optional tameness requirement, assume the closure of $X\setminus P_X$ is a compact subset of an open region carrying the specified smooth two-form and that $J^b$ tames that form there.

There is an actual separable Hilbert ball of smooth paths $J_t(a)$ preserving the protected spatial values, generator charts, boundary structures and optional tameness, such that every derivative of $J(a)-J^b$ at $t=0,1$ vanishes. Finite parameter tangent combinations are dense in every finite coefficient norm in the smooth anti-$J(a)$ fields compactly supported in $(0,1)\times(X\setminus P_X)$. The actual universal strip section is a submersion at every nonconstant finite-energy strip, including those with the same end generator. A dense residual set of parameters makes all these actual strip linearizations surjective in $H^1\to L^2$ and in every integer higher Hilbert Sobolev realization simultaneously.

These auxiliary paths are not asserted to be constant on any endpoint collar. Every one is, however, a smooth coefficient limit of paths $J^{(\epsilon)}$ which are constant on genuine endpoint collars, have the same protected spatial and boundary values and exact generator charts, and retain tameness. No regularity of those approximating paths is asserted here. Transferring regularity to them requires a separate compactness and operator argument; a limit of shrinking collars is not treated as an admissible fixed-collar path.

items.title: Zero-marked bounded-energy strip regularity survives genuine collar approximation
items.scope_note: For every fixed finite E0 this proves existence of original-allowed genuine constant-collar paths regular for all zero-marked strips belowE0, including sameends. It does not provide the separate energy bound for all relevant-index Floer classes, nor address positive-mark bubble strata.
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the nearly symmetric marked strip geometry of the zero-marked bubble-exclusion lemma. In particular all individual boundary curve-system complement components contain marked points, and the almost complex paths have common exact product generator charts, common protected diagonal/region/marked-divisor neighborhoods, and fixed totally real boundary structures. Let $J^*$ be a smooth path in this geometry such that every nonconstant finite-energy zero-marked $J^*$ strip has surjective actual $H^1\to L^2$ linearization. It need not be constant on time-endpoint collars. Fix $E_0<\infty$.

Suppose $J_n\to J^*$ smoothly, with those same fixed geometric structures, including the common generator charts, and uniform nearly symmetric energy constants. Then for all sufficiently large $n$, every zero-marked $J_n$ strip of energy at most $E_0$ has surjective actual linearization. In fact specified right inverses $L^2\to H^1$ can be chosen with one uniform finite bound for all these strips and all sufficiently large $n$, using a fixed smooth target connection flat in the generator charts. Surjectivity also holds in every integer higher Hilbert Sobolev realization.

Consequently a generic auxiliary flat-endpoint-jet path supplied by the flat-jet universal regularity theorem has genuine constant-collar approximating paths which are regular for all zero-marked strips of energy at most this fixed $E_0$. This supplies bounded-energy constant-collar regularity, including same-generator strips. It does not supply a uniform energy bound for all Floer classes of a prescribed index; any such admissibility/domain-index argument remains a separate prerequisite for unrestricted moduli counts or index-two compactifications.

items.title: Actual kernel matching and index additivity along unbubbled strip breaking
items.scope_note: Actual analytic breaking index additivity only. No claim of arbitrary Whitney-class index, Euler/domain formula, finiteness or collar from this module.
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the actual bounded-energy zero-marked sequence and regular limiting geometry of the bounded-energy collar-openness lemma. Pass to the actual unbubbled breaking subsequence there, with its finitely many nonconstant regular levels $v_1,\ldots,v_M$ and translations $q_{j,n}$. Let $D_n$ be the actual $H^1\to L^2$ strip linearization at $u_n$, and $D_j$ that at $v_j$. For all sufficiently large $n$ there are actual real linear isomorphisms
$$\Gamma_n:\bigoplus_{j=1}^M\ker D_j\longrightarrow\ker D_n,$$
with uniformly bounded norms and inverse norms. They are obtained by cutting off and translating component kernel sections, followed by the actual projection $I-Q_nD_n$ using the constructed nearby-solution right inverse. Their difference in operator norm from that cutoff-and-translation map tends to zero. Hence
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}D_n=\sum_{j=1}^M\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}D_j.$$
These are actual operator indices, before longitudinal translation quotient. No identification with a Whitney-class, domain, Euler-measure or relative-grading index is used.

Each level has positive actual index. Thus a sequence of actual index-one strips can have only one level. A sequence of actual index-two strips has at most two levels, and if it has two, each has index one. This assertion does not by itself prove finiteness of the translation quotients or identify the smooth compactification collars.

items.title: Actual zero-marked index-one strips have finite translation quotients below an energy bound
items.scope_note: Finite modulo-two counts of all actual real-index-one zero-marked strips under a fixed finite E0. The limiting path need only be regular at energies≤E0: proof explicitly supplies the finite-level operator argument rather than silently importing the stronger all-energy premise of49/50. No unrestrictedclassenergybound or Maslovidentification supplied.
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the complete marked nearly symmetric geometry, protected neighborhoods and exact product generator charts of the zero-marked bubble-exclusion lemma. Fix $E_0<\infty$, end generators $x_-,x_+$, and an actual smooth path $J_t$ for which every nonconstant zero-marked strip of energy at most $E_0$ has surjective actual linearization. Such a path with genuine endpoint collars is supplied by the bounded-energy collar-openness lemma.

There are finitely many longitudinal-translation orbits of nonconstant zero-marked $J_t$ strips from $x_-$ to $x_+$ with energy at most $E_0$ and real Fredholm index one. This remains true simultaneously over the finite set of ordered end pairs. Their counts modulo two are therefore well-defined integers modulo two. The index is the actual $H^1\to L^2$ operator index, before translation quotient. No identification with a separately named Maslov or domain index is asserted, and the theorem supplies no energy bound for an unrestricted collection of Floer classes.

items.title: Actual unbubbled strip breaking and regular gluing preserve Whitney concatenation
items.scope_note: Full continuous relative-class equality for actual unbubbled breaking and regularpairgluing, not merely divisor-degree or operatorindex additivity. Does not classify arbitrary domains, prove domainindex, or handle bubbles/degenerating targets.
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. In the compact transverse geometry with common exact product generator charts, let an actual sequence of strips have the unbubbled breaking conclusion of the strip compactness theorem, with nonconstant levels $v_1,\ldots,v_M$, matched end generators and no additional energy or image diameter on the intermediate necks or outer tails. Each strip determines its continuous Whitney class by filling its two uniform generator ends, with boundary arcs on $L_0,L_1$. Concatenation joins matching constant end neighborhoods, or equivalently the corresponding marked disk ends.

For all sufficiently large $n$, the actual relative classes satisfy
$$[u_n]=[v_1]*\cdots*[v_M].$$
These are classes under continuous homotopies fixing the two marked ends and preserving each boundary arc. The conclusion uses the actual image collapse and smooth core convergence, not just equality of divisor degrees or energy. It applies in particular to the actual zero-marked unbubbled compactness conclusion, without any additional index hypothesis.

For the actual regular-pair pregluing $u_R$ and Newton-corrected strip $g_R$ in the regular-strip gluing lemma, for all sufficiently large $R$ one has
$$[g_R]=[u_R]=[u^-]*[u^+].$$
No converse classification of relative classes, Maslov/domain formula, or gluing for bubbles or degenerating targets is asserted.

items.title: A fixed zero-marked Whitney class has an actual index-two compactification and mod-two cancellation
items.scope_note: This is actual fixed-zero-mark Whitneyclass compactification/cancellation for generalY geometry, including possible same-generator index2strips. It does not imply finite sums over all indexclasses, nor any positive-mark boundary-degeneration or polygon/target-neck claim. No Maslov/domainEuler identity is substituted for actual classindex.
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Fix the compact nearly symmetric Heegaard geometry with complete marked cut systems, protected diagonal and region-divisor neighborhoods, and common exact product generator charts used in zero-marked bubble exclusion. Every complement component of each individual boundary curve system must contain a marked point. Whitney classes mean continuous two-marked disk relative-homotopy classes with the two boundary arcs on the specified product tori. Their integer $\mu$ is the actual fixed-end Fredholm index constructed by continuous relative smoothing, not a domain Euler formula.

Fix a class $\phi:x\to z$ with $\mu(\phi)=2$ and with all marked divisor degrees zero. Its region divisor degrees $n_R(\phi)$ are well-defined integers. For a common domain-energy constant $C$ put
$$B_\phi=C\sum_R|n_R(\phi)|\int_R\eta.$$
Choose a smooth path with genuine constant endpoint collars, the stipulated protected data, and actual regularity for every nonconstant zero-marked strip of energy at most a number $E_0>B_\phi$. Such paths exist by the auxiliary flat-jet regularity and actual bounded-energy collar-approximation theorems, with $C$ taken uniform in the approximating neighborhood as proved below.

For this path, the moduli space $\widehat{\mathcal M}(\phi)$ of actual strips in $\phi$ modulo longitudinal translation is a Hausdorff second-countable topological one-manifold. It has a compactification by finitely many boundary points. These points are exactly the ordered pairs of actual index-one strip orbits
$$([u],[v]),\qquad u:x\to y,\quad v:y\to z,\quad [u]*[v]=\phi.$$
Each such component has zero marked degrees and energy at most $B_\phi$. Each boundary point has the actual one-sided gluing collar with smooth interior from the regular-pair collar theorem. No differentiability at a prescribed compactifying parameter is asserted.

The number of these boundary points is even. Equivalently the sum modulo two of the products of rigid counts over the factorizations $\phi=\phi_1*\phi_2$ with $\mu(\phi_1)=\mu(\phi_2)=1$ is zero; only finitely many factors with nonzero counts occur. This is the cancellation identity for this fixed zero-marked class. It does not establish finiteness over all classes of prescribed index, a domain-index formula, positive-marked boundary-degeneration cancellation, or polygon/target-degeneration gluing.

items.title: The constant transverse strip has an actual weighted boundary-node inverse
items.scope_note: Actual framedconstantstrip linearproblem only; q0nodevalue is an asymptoticcoordinate, q≥1genuinecontinuousvalue. No node-evaluation directions on its zero kernel, no boundarydiskregularity/nonlineargluing/count assertion.
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. On $S=\mathbb R\times[0,1]$ take $D_0=\partial_s+i\partial_t$ with target $\mathbb C^m$, $m\ge1$, lower boundary $\mathbb R^m$ and upper boundary $i\mathbb R^m$. Its two infinite ends have fixed zero limits. Remove the boundary point $p=(0,0)$, write $z=s+it$ near it, and choose its holomorphic cylindrical coordinate
$$z=-e^{-\pi\zeta},\qquad\zeta=\sigma+i\tau,\quad\sigma>\sigma_0,\quad0\le\tau\le1.$$
Both edges of this new end have real boundary values. Fix $0<\delta<\pi$ and an integer $q\ge0$.

Define $\mathcal X_{q,\delta}^{\mathrm{node}}$ as the actual weak section space with the stated zeroth real boundary traces, ordinary $H^{q+1}$ norm outside a smaller node half-disk (including both unweighted infinite strip ends), and on the node end an expansion
$$\xi=c+v,\qquad c\in\mathbb R^m,\qquad e^{\delta\sigma}v\in H^{q+1}.$$
Use the square root of the sum of those squared norms and $|c|^2$ with fixed overlap cutoffs; do not impose additional higher normal traces or a higher-norm smooth-closure condition. Define $\mathcal Y_{q,\delta}^{\mathrm{node}}$ by ordinary $H^q$ off that half-disk and the rescaled forcing condition
$$f_{\mathrm{cyl}}(\zeta)=\overline{z'(\zeta)}f(z(\zeta)),\qquad e^{\delta\sigma}f_{\mathrm{cyl}}\in H^q.$$
Use the analogous square-sum norm on the target. These are Hilbert spaces with equivalent choices of fixed overlap cutoffs. The actual operator
$$D_0:\mathcal X_{q,\delta}^{\mathrm{node}}\longrightarrow\mathcal Y_{q,\delta}^{\mathrm{node}}$$
is a bounded real isomorphism, with a bounded inverse $Q_{q,\delta}$. Its free-node Fredholm index is zero, and its kernel is zero. The asymptotic constant $c$ is a bounded linear evaluation on its full domain; for $q\ge1$ it is the genuine continuous value at the filled boundary point. For $q=0$ it means the specified weighted asymptotic constant, not an asserted pointwise trace on arbitrary $H^1$ sections.

For the fixed-node subspace $c=0$, the same operator has zero kernel and closed range of real codimension $m$, with index $-m$. More precisely
$$\Lambda_{q,\delta}(f)=\operatorname{ev}_p Q_{q,\delta}f$$
is bounded and onto $\mathbb R^m$, and its kernel is exactly that range. Restricting $Q_{q,\delta}$ to this kernel gives its bounded range inverse. Thus imposing a node value is a genuine finite-dimensional constraint on this constant-strip problem, rather than an assumption of node-evaluation surjectivity on its zero kernel. No boundary-disk regularity, nonlinear attachment gluing or degeneration count is asserted.

items.title: Actual node-fixed boundary-disk charts, affine slices, and the cover index
items.scope_note: Actual operator-surjectivity premise retained: no genericity, all-nonsimple-factorization theorem, boundarydiskcount, compactification or attachmentgluing asserted. Configuration is unionofactualsmooth-referencecharts, not unproved H3 approximation of everyroughconstrainedmap.
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $X$ have real dimension $2m$, $m\ge1$, and be the compact target in the actual boundary-preserving local-addition theorem, let $L$ be one of its oriented product tori, and let $x$ be a generator. Let $J$ be a smooth autonomous almost complex structure for which $L$ is totally real. Near $x$ require one fixed chart taking $J$ to $i$, $L$ to $\mathbb R^m$ and $x$ to zero. Fix a boundary point $p$ of the disk.

There is an actual second-countable Hilbert manifold, constructed as the union of local-addition charts at smooth boundary-compatible node-fixed references, of $H^3$ disk maps with boundary in $L$ and value $x$ at $p$. It contains all smooth such maps; no approximation assertion for every arbitrary constrained rough map is required. Near a smooth reference map its model is the space of $H^3$ sections with the zeroth $TL$ boundary trace and $\xi(p)=0$, intersected with the actual $H^1$ completed boundary domain, not an asserted higher-norm smooth closure. The Cauchy–Riemann expression is an actual smooth $H^2$ section; its zeros are smooth maps. If the boundary determinant winding of the full disk problem is $k$, its actual full linearization has real index $m+2k$, and its node-fixed realization has index $2k$. Write $\mu=2k$ for this actual node-fixed operator index.

At a smooth zero, compact node-fixed surjectivity is equivalent to surjectivity of the actual weighted node-fixed punctured-disk realization, for every integer order and each weight $0<\delta<\pi$. No surjectivity is assumed without this explicit operator condition. At a nonconstant zero satisfying it, the actual node-fixed zero space is locally a smooth $\mu$-dimensional manifold. The explicit positive affine group $z\mapsto az+b$, $a>0$, $b\in\mathbb R$, of holomorphic half-plane automorphisms fixing infinity acts freely and properly, and smoothly on this regular zero manifold. Its quotient has local smooth slices of dimension $\mu-2$. In particular when $\mu=2$ every regular such disk is locally isolated modulo these automorphisms. No global count or compactness is concluded.

Finally if $u=v\circ\psi$ for a smooth degree-$d$ disk map $\psi$ taking boundary to boundary and the marked point to the marked point, then $\mu(u)=d\mu(v)$ for the corresponding actual Cauchy–Riemann-symbol indices. In particular a disk of actual node-fixed index two cannot be a nontrivial proper holomorphic disk cover of degree $d>1$: the oriented torus makes $\mu(v)$ even. This does not assert that every nonsimple disk admits such a covering factorization, or prove generic regularity, boundary-degeneration classification, gluing or cancellation.

items.title: Actual generic node-fixed regularity for disks with dense interior injective points
items.scope_note: Dense set of actual globally unique interior preimages is an explicit retained geometric hypothesis. Neither somewhere-injective equivalence nor index2 factorization/classification is asserted. Genericity is proved on actual diskconfiguration/universalFredholm setup, not assumed moduli axioms.
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use the compact target and one oriented product torus $L$ of the actual node-fixed disk-chart lemma. Fix a smooth autonomous background $J^b$, totally real on $L$, and finitely many disjoint compact generator neighborhoods $A_x$ inside larger exact background charts taking $J^b$ to $i$ and $L$ to $\mathbb R^m$. Choose smaller working generator charts with closures inside $\operatorname{Int}(A_x)$. Let $D$ be compact and disjoint from $L\cup\bigcup_xA_x$, containing any protected diagonal or divisor neighborhoods. Put $P_X=D\cup L\cup\bigcup_xA_x$. For optional tameness assume the closure of $X\setminus P_X$ is a compact subset of a smooth two-form's open taming region and that $J^b$ tames it there.

There is an actual separable Hilbert ball of smooth autonomous structures $J(a)$ preserving all values on $P_X$, the smaller working charts and optional tameness. A dense residual subset of its parameters has the following property, simultaneously for all the finitely many node values $x$: every nonconstant $J(a)$ disk with boundary on $L$, marked boundary value $x$, and dense set
$$I(u)=\{z\in\mathbb D^\circ:du(z)\ne0,\ u^{-1}(u(z))=\{z\}\}$$
of interior injective points has surjective actual compact node-fixed $H^3\to H^2$ linearization. It is also surjective in every weighted node-fixed realization at weights $0<\delta<\pi$ and every integer order. The actual universal derivative is onto at every such disk, not merely postulated to be onto.

The density hypothesis on $I(u)$ is retained. No equivalence with a weaker somewhere-injective condition is asserted. In particular the index-two cover obstruction does not alone prove this hypothesis for every disk. The result supplies neither generic regularity of all boundary degenerations, their global count, nor attachment gluing or cancellation.

items.title: Real oval divisors exclude holomorphic spheres in symmetric products
items.scope_note: Actual supplied real Riemann surface with at leastm+1fixedovals anddistinctdivisorentries. No assertion suchstructureexists forarbitrarydiagram; no nearlysymmetricdeformationopenness, sphereindex, diskfactorization, or degenerationcount.
items.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a connected closed Riemann surface, $m\ge1$, and $D=p_1+\cdots+p_m$ a divisor with pairwise distinct entries. If there is a nonconstant holomorphic map $u:\mathbb {CP}^1\to\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$ for the standard complex symmetric-product structure whose image contains $D$, then there is a nonconstant meromorphic function on $\Sigma$ all of whose poles are simple and belong to $\{p_1,\ldots,p_m\}$. Some of these entries may not be poles.

Suppose in addition that $\Sigma$ has an antiholomorphic involution $\rho$ with at least $m+1$ pairwise disjoint embedded circles in its fixed set, and that $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ lie on different such circles. Then no meromorphic function as above exists, and no nonconstant standard holomorphic sphere passes through $D$. This is a statement about the supplied real Riemann surface and divisor: it does not construct such a complex structure for a given attaching system, assert avoidance for nearby almost-complex structures, or compute any sphere index or degeneration count.
